description: This case study is the Australian Energy Market Operator's final report on the black system event in South Australia on 28 September 2016, published in March 2017 as a 273-page consolidation of its three preliminary reports. It covers the pre-event status of the South Australian system, the sequence of events in the 87 seconds before system shutdown at 16:18:16, the restoration steps, system restart ancillary services, the suspension of the market until 11 October 2016, recommendations and next steps for power system security in a changing generation mix; about 850,000 customers lost supply. Access: free PDF download from AEMO; the report carries AEMO copyright and a disclaimer but no open licence. Coverage is the South Australian region of the National Electricity Market. Caveats: only the introduction and executive summary were read, and the causes, wind farm behaviour and count of recommendations come from search summaries. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of grids with high wind penetration, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: About 850,000 South Australian customers lost supply. The report sets out the pre-event system state, the sequence of events in the 87 seconds before shutdown, restoration, system restart ancillary services, market suspension until 11 October 2016, and recommendations. Search summaries add that severe weather damaged transmission assets, wind farm protection settings and loss of the Heywood interconnector figured in the outcome, and that AEMO made 19 recommendations.
